interpretations.decision: MCP Streamable HTTP via mcp 1.30.0 StreamableHTTPSessionManager(stateless=True, json_response=False, no event store) behind an Atlas raw-ASGI wrapper with the exact endpoint /mcp and POST only. It is the only SDK mode in which a client disconnect cancels the in-flight handler

The same fixture index is served by a stdio child and an HTTP child (CLI path). Initialize result, tools/list digest, resources lists, ping, tool results for steps 7-16 (text bytes, isError, structuredContent) and the -32601 error are equal at 2025-11-25 and 2024-11-05, plus a live page/resources-read step. The HTTP shaping revision comes from the mcp-protocol-version header via negotiate(); an absent header is 2025-03-26, as in the SDK

resolve_loopback requires every getaddrinfo result to be loopback (IPv4-mapped unwrapped; wildcard, scope id and mixed results rejected). The literal is bound, never the name. It is enforced at the CLI (UsageError, exit 2) and again in run_http, plus a post-bind getsockname check. There is no public-bind option until S40

A client TCP close during a gated structured query cancels the handler; the per-request reader (ExitStack) closes and its source lease fd is released. Disconnect = cancellation is a documented deviation from the spec's guidance; stateless notifications/cancelled is a no-op. Synchronous legacy ops, view_file and list_dir cannot be cancelled mid-call and are bounded by their caps

An in-flight gate rejects (503, Retry-After: 1, JSON-RPC -32000, reason inflight_limit) before any body read and never queues. Each admitted POST holds a refcounted ticket, reached through the ASGI scope, until both the HTTP exchange and every Atlas handler for it have ended, so the cancellation unwind cannot push active work over the limit. Verified independently through concurrent reader leases and the traversal hook

The wrapper order is peer loopback (403), Host (421), Origin (403; absent passes; exact scheme://host[:port] allowlist; * and null rejected), path (404), method (405), admission (503), then the SDK body cap (413). A rejection happens before the SDK manager runs, which spies and withheld-body requests prove

A neighborhood request that stops on a deterministic limit (visited_node_limit, never deadline), retried after a disconnected attempt, yields byte-identical SSE data lines and equal frontier commitments on two HTTP requests
